clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, presented at 31 weeks gestation with right shoulder pain (triggered by lifting her 11-month-old child), persistent dyspnea since her first pregnancy 1.5 years prior, and new-onset cough and hemoptysis during the current pregnancy. Chest X-ray revealed a tumor mass in the right lung in close relation to the scapula. MRI of the cranium and thorax identified multiple highly suspicious lesions: right lung mass, mediastinal involvement, inferior angle of right scapula with soft tissue component, and osteolytic lesion of the 3rd thoracic vertebral body with dural and spinal nerve involvement. A fine-needle biopsy of the pulmonary tumor mass was obtained via bronchoscopy. Cesarean section was performed, followed by open biopsy of the right scapula lesion. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of NUT midline carcinoma by immunohistochemistry, despite negative standard FISH due to cryptic NUT translocation. Post-delivery PET-CT demonstrated multiple metastases in bilateral breasts in addition to the known lung and scapula lesions, confirming stage IV disseminated disease. Palliative systemic chemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m²)/carboplatin (AUC 6) was initiated by the oncology clinic, with ovarian protection (Trenantone® 130 mg subcutaneously) and osteoprotective bisphosphonate therapy (Zometa® 4 mg). Radiotherapy was planned for bone metastases. After five courses of chemotherapy, the patient demonstrated clinical improvement with decline of dyspnea, and PET-CT at 3 months showed partial remission of metastases in the right lung and bilateral breasts.

final.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, presented at 31 weeks gestation with right shoulder pain (triggered by lifting her 11-month-old child), persistent dyspnea since her first pregnancy 1.5 years prior, and new-onset cough and hemoptysis during the current pregnancy. Chest X-ray revealed a tumor mass in the right lung in close relation to the scapula. MRI of the cranium and thorax identified multiple highly suspicious lesions: right lung mass, mediastinal involvement, inferior angle of right scapula with soft tissue component, and osteolytic lesion of the 3rd thoracic vertebral body with dural and spinal nerve involvement. A fine-needle biopsy of the pulmonary tumor mass was obtained via bronchoscopy. Cesarean section was performed, followed by open biopsy of the right scapula lesion. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of NUT midline carcinoma by immunohistochemistry, despite negative standard FISH due to cryptic NUT translocation. Post-delivery PET-CT demonstrated multiple metastases in bilateral breasts in addition to the known lung and scapula lesions, confirming stage IV disseminated disease. Palliative systemic chemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m²)/carboplatin (AUC 6) was initiated by the oncology clinic, with ovarian protection (Trenantone® 130 mg subcutaneously) and osteoprotective bisphosphonate therapy (Zometa® 4 mg). Radiotherapy was planned for bone metastases. After five courses of chemotherapy, the patient demonstrated clinical improvement with decline of dyspnea, and PET-CT at 3 months showed partial remission of metastases in the right lung and bilateral breasts.
